competitive Lotka–Volterra equations are a simple model of the [population dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_dynamics) of species competing for some common resource.

Conservation genetics is an [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinary) subfield of [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) that aims to understand the dynamics of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s in a population for the purpose of [natural resource management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_resource_management), conservation of [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity), and the prevention of species [extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction).

Conservation paleobiology is a field of [paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology) that applies the knowledge of the geological and paleoecological record to the [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology) and restoration of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) and [ecosystem services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem_services).

Conservation Physiology is an online only, fully open access journal published by [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press) on behalf of the [Society for Experimental Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Experimental_Biology).

Conservation psychology is the scientific study of the reciprocal relationships between [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and the rest of [nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature), with a particular focus on how to encourage [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_movement) of the [natural world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment).

conservation status of a [group of organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon) (for example, a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)) indicates whether the group still exists and how likely it is to become [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) in [the near future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction_debt).
Conservation-induced extinction is where efforts to save [endangered species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_species) lead to the extinction of other species.

Conservation-reliant species are animal or plant [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that require continuing species-specific [wildlife management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildlife_management) intervention such as [[Hunting#Wildlife management|predator control]], [habitat management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat_conservation) and [parasite control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest_control) to survive, even when a self-sustainable recovery in population is achieved.

constructed wetland is an artificial [wetland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetland) to treat [sewage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sewage), [greywater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greywater), [stormwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormwater) runoff or [industrial wastewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_wastewater_treatment).

Construction costs is a concept in biology that conveys how much [glucose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucose) is required to construct a unit of plant biomass, given the biosynthetic pathways and starting from glucose and mineral constituents.
consumer in a [food chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_chain) is a living creature that eats organisms from a different population.

consumer-resource models (CRMs) are a class of [ecological model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_model)s in which a [community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_(ecology)) of consumer species compete for a common pool of resources.

contest competition refers to a situation where available resources, such as food and mates, are utilized only by one or a few individuals, thus preventing development or reproduction of other individuals.

continental divide is a [drainage divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_divide) on a [continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent) such that the [drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin) on one side of the divide feeds into one [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean) or [sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea), and the basin on the other side either feeds into a different ocean or sea, or else is [endorheic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endorheic_basin), not connected to the open sea.
continental shelf is a portion of a [continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent) that is submerged under an area of relatively shallow water, known as a shelf sea.

continental shelf pump is proposed to operate in the shallow waters of the [continental shelves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf), acting as a mechanism to transport [carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon) (as either dissolved or particulate material) from surface waters to the interior of the adjacent deep ocean.

littoral zone, also called litoral or nearshore, is the part of an [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean), [sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea), [lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake), or [river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River), that is close to the [shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shore).

definition: living stump is created when a live [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree) is cut, burned, eaten, or infected, causing its [cambium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambium) to die above the root system.

local biodiversity action plan (LBAP, pronounced 'ell-bap') is a plan aimed at conserving the fauna, flora and habitats – collectively referred to as [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity) – of a defined area, usually along [local authority boundary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_government_in_England) lines.

Local food is food that is produced within a short distance of where it is consumed, often accompanied by a social structure and supply chain different from the large-scale supermarket [system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_system).

Local Futures (formerly the International Society for Ecology and Culture) is a [non-profit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-profit) organization whose purpose is to raise awareness about what it identifies as the root causes of contemporary social, environmental, and economic crises.
log jam is a naturally occurring phenomenon characterized by a dense accumulation of tree trunks and pieces of large wood across a vast section of a river, stream, or lake.

definition: Long-Term Agroecosystem Research (LTAR) Network is a project to understand and enhance the sustainability of agriculture through coordinated research and long-term study.

longleaf pine ecosystem is a [temperate coniferous forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperate_coniferous_forest) ecosystem found within the [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States).

Lotka–Volterra equations, also known as the Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model, are a pair of first-order [nonlinear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear) [differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_equation)s, frequently used to describe the [dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_system) of [biological systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology) in which two species interact, one as a [predator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predator) and the other as prey.
Lottery competition in [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) is a model for how organisms [compete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competition_(biology)).

Luca Casarini (born 8 May 1967) is an Italian activist and former proponent of the [Tute Bianche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tute_Bianche) movement.

Lydie Massard (born 24 August 1978) is a French politician of the [Breton Democratic Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breton_Democratic_Union) who served as a [Member of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament) from 2023 to 2024.

Plant Resources of Tropical Africa, known by its acronym PROTA, is a retired NGO and interdisciplinary documentation programme active between 2000 and 2013.
